title: Generics
explain: Generics let one function or type work with many types while keeping them connected. The `<T>` is a placeholder that is filled in from how you call the function. Use them when the output type depends on the input type, such as `first<T>(items: T[]): T`.
exercise: Write a generic `last<T>` function and a generic `Pair<A, B>` type, then use both.
tip: Don't add a generic when a plain type works. If `T` appears only once in the signature, it usually isn't doing anything.
